The claimed inversion does not survive full resolution. In all three seeds the outer silhouette (shoulders, outer arms, sleeve edges, hem, hands) is drawn with a near-black ink contour that is clearly the heaviest, darkest mark in the image; the interior fold/hatch marks are thin, light grey, delicate hairlines. Zoomed 2-3x crops of the left/right shoulder and sleeve edges show this unambiguously for seeds 1001 and 2002, and the seed-3003 full frame shows the same bold silhouette against faint interior marks.

Quantitative confirmation (garment band, dark-run scan per row, threshold bg-45): outer contour runs vs interior runs — P7000214 outer meanW 4.40 px / mean min-luminance 31 vs interior meanW 3.89 / 91; P7000215 outer 8.25 / 27 vs interior 4.54 / 91; P7000216 outer 6.91 / 29 vs interior 3.21 / 100. The outer contour is both wider and roughly 60-70 luminance levels darker than any interior stroke, i.e. the opposite of "thin light-grey outer, dense dark interior".

Explanation of the thumbnail artifact: the outer contour is a fine 2-3 px ink line sitting against a mid-grey (bg ~181-192) studio ground, so downsampling blends it toward light grey and drops its weight, while the many delicate interior hatch strokes aggregate into apparent interior density. Seed 1001 is the busiest interior of the three (slightly more hatching than a strict reading of "sparse"), but the strokes are delicate and light and the bold outer contour still dominates, so it is not a defect. limited_two_tone (grey top + cream/olive bottom) and subtle_contact_shadow read as the reviewer already noted. Saturation was not the concern, so saturation_screen.json was not the deciding evidence.

The hold claimed the garment contour is "a thin near-uniform grey line with no legible pressure swelling or tapering." At full resolution that is false on all three seeds, and the three seeds agree (no seed disagreement to arbitrate).

Seed 1001: the outer sleeve contour swells monotonically from the shoulder to the cuff — sub-pixel slope-corrected ink mass along the left sleeve contour rises from ~1.1 at the upper sleeve to ~3.3 near the cuff (roughly 3x). Interior fold strokes on the sleeve and shoulder enter as fine hairlines, swell mid-stroke, and taper to points.
Seeds 2002 and 3003: same behaviour at the weight-bearing locations — the elbow-crease and cuff-fold strokes each enter thin, swell in the crease, and taper to hairline terminals, while the straight forearm run of the contour stays thin. The contour is dark near-black, not grey.

Control comparison confirms this is real modulation and not the incidental wobble any generated line has. Rendering P7000450 (crisp_uniform + transparent_glaze + reflected_color, seed 3003 — the deliberately even-weight linework value) at the identical crop and zoom shows a genuinely constant-thickness contour from shoulder to cuff with no swelling and no tapering. That is what "near-uniform" actually looks like, and case_162 does not look like it.

Note on method: the automated stroke-mass statistic is NOT a usable discriminator here and I did not rely on it for the verdict — median smoothed max/min ratio is 2.86 for crisp_uniform, 3.30 for elastic_pressure, 3.23 for fine_tapered, because the leftmost-dark-run scan picks up hair and is confounded by contour curvature. The verdict rests on direct visual inspection of the full-resolution crops against the crisp_uniform control.

Saturation was not the concern, but the screen is clean anyway: this item is in the airy_pastel group (median 0.0839, range 0.0672-0.1085), which has outlier_count 0, and the whole screen has outlier_total 0. The item appears in no outlier list.

The defect was a 256px downsampling artifact: the pressure modulation lives in a 1-3px stroke-width range, which the contact-sheet tile collapses into a single flat grey pixel line.
